prompt: We need a clear product requirements document for a self-service account data export in Northstar, for Product, Legal, Support, and Engineering to review. Read the material in this folder and turn it into implementable requirements covering scope, access, delivery, limits, security, and unresolved points. Keep decisions tied to the source material and call out assumptions where the material is incomplete. Put the result at docs/requirements.md. End the file with a ```json block of the form {"requirements": [{"id": "R1", "text": "..."}], "assumptions": ["..."]}.

facts.answer: Only an account owner or a user granted the Account Data Export permission may submit an export request; Support agents cannot submit one for a customer.
Deliver a ZIP archive with CSV data files and a JSON manifest. All exported date-times must use UTC with a trailing Z.
Exclude payment card numbers, Northstar internal support notes, and records deleted before the request. Customer-visible appointment records, including cancelled appointments, remain in scope.
Start processing within 15 minutes of a valid request and make the completed package available within 72 hours.
The signed download link expires 7 days after the package becomes ready; after that, the customer must submit a new request.
The compressed archive limit is 2 GB. If a package would exceed that limit, route the customer to Support rather than splitting it automatically.
Self-service export is available on Pro and Enterprise plans, not Starter.
Write export.requested, export.ready, export.downloaded, and export.expired to the immutable audit log, retained for 400 days.

scriptedUser.defaultReply: I'm not sure, use your judgement.

checks.cmd: node -e "const fs=require('fs'); const t=fs.readFileSync('docs/requirements.md','utf8'); const f=String.fromCharCode(96).repeat(3); const i=t.lastIndexOf(f+'json'); if(i<0) process.exit(1); const j=JSON.parse(t.slice(t.indexOf('\n',i)+1,t.lastIndexOf(f)).trim()); if(!Array.isArray(j.requirements)||j.requirements.length<5||j.requirements.some(r=>!r.id)) process.exit(1);"

rubric.criterion: Requirements distinguish customer-visible scope from Northstar-only material and explain the resulting product behavior. Fail: the archive scope is stated loosely ('all data'), or it includes Northstar internal support notes or payment card numbers. Partial: internal notes and card numbers are excluded, but the other scope rules are missing: records deleted before the request are excluded, cancelled appointments stay in scope, other tenants and secrets are kept out, UTC times with a trailing Z. Pass: the document defines the customer record families in the archive, excludes payment card numbers, Northstar internal support notes and records deleted before the request, keeps cancelled appointments in, and states who may request (an account owner or a user with the Account Data Export permission, not Support), the plan limit (Pro and Enterprise, not Starter) and the reason for each exclusion. (code cannot check this because semantic scope and rationale require human review)

Assumptions and open points are honest about decisions that the source folder does not settle. Fail: the assumptions list is empty or restates decided facts, or an invented decision is written as settled (for example splitting an archive over 2 GB). Partial: some assumptions are listed, but they are generic, or a decided limit (the one active background job, the 72-hour delivery, the 7-day link expiry, the 2 GB archive limit with a route to Support) is shown as an open question. Pass: the assumptions name what the folder does not settle, each says what the requirement depends on it, and the decided limits are written as requirements. (code cannot check this because it cannot judge whether uncertainty was represented faithfully)

The final message says plainly what was delivered, what was assumed and what is still open, without claiming more than the files show. Fail: the message says the work is complete or settled while the decisions the folder does not settle stay unmentioned, or it does not say that docs/requirements.md was written. Partial: it names docs/requirements.md and what it holds, but lists no assumptions, or leaves out the decisions the folder does not settle. Pass: it names docs/requirements.md and its closing JSON block, lists the assumptions made, says the decisions the folder does not settle still need an answer or a check, and claims nothing the files do not show. (code cannot check this because the message is free text about the work)

verdicts.note: The prompt describes the desired outcome (requirements document with specific sections and format) without prescribing methods, frameworks, or processes.

The prompt clearly specifies scope areas (scope, access, delivery, limits, security, unresolved points), output path, and JSON structure; hidden tests check for factual claims from scripted facts and grounded fixture content.
Eight facts must be discovered through questions; fixture has intentional gaps (no authority, no SLA, no audit vocabulary, plan eligibility unclear) that require synthesis and inquiry.
All fact topics are discoverable through natural questions (who can request, file format, exclusions, deadlines, expiry, size limits, plan eligibility, audit); reference scores 100%.
Fixture documents contain gaps and explicitly state what they do NOT define; all key numbers (15 min, 72 hrs, 7 days, 2 GB, 400 days) are only in scripted facts, not in fixture.

items.note: Prompt asks to read material and create implementable requirements, no specific method prescribed.
Fixture contains admin roles, data schemas, policy notes but not synthesized requirements.
Hidden tests check patterns matching scripted facts; rubric matches prompt and fixture scope.
Competent PM could extract requirements from fixture; alternative wording/structure would pass.
